summary: The Controller update helper consumes each GUI update request before reading it, reads it without following links or blocking and accepts only nex-controller from an http(s) URL without control characters, releases it on every failure including unexpected errors, writes progress through a symlink-safe file handed to the Controller's user, and clears requests queued during a successful apply; postinst restarts the service unless the helper is running, clears stale requests and their progress text, and resets a start-limited update path unit, so one failed update no longer wedges every later update (BUG-0193). API impact: none — the updates API and pending request format are unchanged.

guide.reason: Software updates guide explains the stuck 'Update requested…' state and the one-time recovery for Controllers on 0.2.5 or earlier.

api.reason: API impact: none. GET /api/v1/updates and POST /api/v1/updates/apply are unchanged; the Controller still writes the same pending-update.json; only the root helper's handling and file ownership change.

roadmap.reason: Bug fix in the existing Controller update path.

state.reason: No product state added; the request, marker and progress files are transient update plumbing on the Controller VM.

verification.method: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' (each new test in ControllerUpdateHelperRecoveryTests failed against the unfixed helper or an earlier draft). Native, disposable Debian systemd VM: the published 0.2.5 package wedged as reported; the final 0.2.6 package cleared the wedge on install, rejected an injected repo_url without touching the APT source, and ran a normal failing request exactly once with the path unit staying active and readable progress; the preceding 0.2.6 build showed a planted symlink not followed and a stale marker cleared by reinstall.
